item.title: Weaviate Launches Agent Skills for Developers
item.description:
Weaviate Launches Agent Skills for Developers

Weaviate introduces Agent Skills to empower developers building AI applications.

🔍 Overview

  • Agent Skills to empower developers building AI applications with Weaviate.
  • Agent Skills to help developers build and use AI agents with Weaviate more effectively.
  • Each skill is a folder containing instructions, scripts, and resources that agents like Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and others can discover to work more accurately and efficiently.
  • The skill is automatically discovered by compatible agents.

🧩 How it works

  • Works with any agent that supports the Agent Skills format.
  • Utility functions for the agent to directly interact with a Weaviate database.
  • Blueprints for complete end-to-end AI applications with state-of-the art guidelines for agentic infrastructure.
  • Use weaviate-best-practices to write or review Weaviate application code, with guidance on schema design, batch imports, and search.

⚙️ Key details

  • Each skill is a folder containing instructions, scripts, and resources.
  • The scripts and cookbooks rely on widely adopted third-party packages.
  • Not responsible for security of third-party components; new vulnerabilities may arise.
  • Users should run own security scans before executing any code and review packages flagged for known issues.
  • It is recommended to create a free cluster in the weaviate console.

🚀 Availability

  • Python 3.11+ required.
  • A Weaviate Cloud instance is needed.

🛠️ Capabilities

  • Create Collections
  • Explore Collections (Aggregation, Metadata, Schema)
  • Query Collections (Keyword-, Vector-, Hybrid Search) (Support filters)
  • Import Data (supports multi-vector and PDF ingestion)
  • Multimodal PDF Ingestion
  • Data Explorer
  • Retrieval Augmented Generation (Basic, Advanced, Agentic)
  • Query Agent
  • Query Agent Chatbot
  • Build a chatbot using the Query Agent
  • Build a multimodal RAG app for my PDF documents
  • Build an agentic RAG app
  • Search my Weaviate documentation for information about HNSW indexing
  • List all my Weaviate collections
  • Find products similar to ‘wireless headphones’ in the Products collection

📚 Examples

  • Search my Weaviate documentation for information about HNSW indexing.
  • List all my Weaviate collections.
  • Find products similar to ‘wireless headphones’ in the Products collection.
  • Build a chatbot using the Query Agent.

#Weaviate #AIagents #DeveloperTools #RAG #AgentSkills

Source: weaviate/agent-skills

item.title: Pydantic AI Skills Enhances Agent Capabilities with Progressive Disclosure
item.description:
Pydantic AI Skills Enhances Agent Capabilities with Progressive Disclosure

Pydantic AI Skills introduces enhanced capabilities for Agent Skills, supporting progressive disclosure and modular packages of instructions, resources, and scripts. This update allows agents to handle specialized tasks more efficiently by loading only the necessary resources when needed.

🔍 Overview

  • Pydantic AI Skills enhances Agent Skills with progressive disclosure.
  • Supports filesystem and programmatic skills.
  • Enables remote skill registries and bundled-file execution.

🧩 How it works

  • Agent Skills are modular packages of instructions, resources, and scripts.
  • On disk, a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file, reference documents, and executable scripts.
  • Your agent starts with only the name and description of each skill.
  • When a task calls for a skill, it loads the full instructions and resources only if needed.
  • This is progressive disclosure, allowing the skill library to grow without every skill paying for space in the prompt.

⚙️ Key details

  • pydantic-ai-harness ships a Skills capability that reads SKILL.md packages from local directories.
  • pydantic-ai-skills is the companion that fills the gaps, including remote registries and bundled-file execution.
  • Remote registries support Git and S3 sources, with composition features.
  • Bundled files can be read or executed with read_skill_resource and run_skill_script.
  • Sandboxed execution keeps untrusted scripts off the host.
  • ${SKILL_DIR} resolution substitutes the path in scripts.
  • Programmatic skills can be defined in Python within the same catalog.
  • v2 introduces SkillsToolset, SkillsDirectory, reload(), and tools for listing and loading skills.
  • Each skill becomes its own deferred capability, with names and descriptions acting as fields the runtime uses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Progressive disclosure allows the skill library to grow without every skill paying for space in the prompt.
  • Enhanced capabilities for handling specialized tasks more efficiently.
  • Supports remote skill registries and bundled-file execution.
  • Sandboxed execution ensures security for untrusted scripts.

#PydanticAI #AgentSkills #ProgressiveDisclosure #AIAgents #AITools

Source: DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills

item.title: LearnPrompt and associated agent skills gain 800+ GitHub stars
item.description:
LearnPrompt and associated agent skills gain 800+ GitHub stars

LearnPrompt, described as the account’s earliest public project, has been updated with a suite of agent skills and automated tools. The project recently reached a milestone of 800+ stars within one month of launch. The update includes the AI News Radar’s ‘伯乐’ skill, which automated the maintenance of the radar tool, and a new collection of 14 installable Agent Skills designed for heavy agent users.

🧩 Core Features

The ecosystem now centers on several key tools:

  • AI News Radar: Utilizes GitHub Actions, web interfaces, and automated summaries to monitor AI and tech information sources. It determines the value of new sources via a 7-day cooling-off period, checks for content duplication, and identifies stable integration methods. Its first application was upgrading ai-news-radar from v0.6 to v0.7.0, merging 4 PRs in a single dialogue.
  • Information Monitoring Methodology: Establishes a public method for monitoring information sources that involves fixed scraping criteria, daily snapshots, historical comparisons, and report generation, with results posted to a GitHub Pages site.
  • 淘金小镇: Tracks daily AI skill trends starting from ClawHub Top 100, expanding to monitor update logs (e.g., Claude Code) and model leaderboards (e.g., AA Index) with minimal environment dependencies.
  • Humanize PPT: Processes over 50 TED speeches to analyze main themes, audience perception, and narrative order before generating PPT content.

🧩 Installable Agent Skills

The update includes 14 installable skills that transform agent workflows into public, verifiable assets:

Skill Name Function
鲁班 Refines usable skills into installable, distributable, and verifiable public assets.
庖丁 Dissects viral content strategies without API usage, distilling them into installable content coaching.
蔡伦 Converts dialogue conclusions into shareable one-page documents in 3 seconds.
阿福 Manages the Obsidian inbox, linking items directly to the calendar.
愚公 Automates agent loops to handle long tasks without manual prompting.
搭子 Coordinates Claude Code for planning/review and Codex for implementation/closure, using a Session Receipt for logging.
Irasutoya配图 Converts key judgments from articles into Irasutoya-style reaction character images.
CC Harness六件套 Provides memory, compression, verification, and scheduling for heavy agent users via a single command.
bugu Reports agent status via vocal cues during long tasks.
carl-weread Recommends book sections based on user blockers.
x-article-publisher Converts Feishu documents into X Articles in one click.

The collection also includes automated research loops, idea files, LLM simulation debates, meta-reflection, and behavioral guidelines for code writing.

💡 Context

LearnPrompt serves as a continuously maintained Chinese AI learning path covering topics such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, prompt engineering, ChatGPT, RAG, Agents, AI programming, Agent Skills, Obsidian, Midjourney, Runway, Stable Diffusion, digital humans, AI voice/music, and large model fine-tuning.

item.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills standard to Agentic AI Foundation
item.description:
Anthropic donates Agent Skills standard to Agentic AI Foundation

On 22 October 2026 Anthropic announced that it is donating its Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), which resides under the Linux Foundation.

🔍 Overview

  • Anthropic today released a news post confirming the donation.
  • The donation moves the Agent Skills specification to a neutral, community‑driven body.

🤝 Donation Details

  • The standard is being handed to the Agentic AI Foundation, the organization Anthropic co‑founded with Block and OpenAI last year.
  • AAIF also hosts the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which Anthropic donated earlier.
  • Anthropic’s statement: “We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community‑driven, and vendor‑neutral.”

📜 Open‑Standard Commitment

  • Anthropic first described Agent Skills as an open standard in December 2025.
  • The same blog author verified the donation intent by querying Claude through the datasette‑mcp plugin.

🏛️ Governance

  • AAIF operates under the Linux Foundation, providing a vendor‑neutral home for specifications like Agent Skills and MCP.
  • Anthropic expects the standard to reside permanently within AAIF, “the new home of the MCP specification.”

#Anthropic #AgentSkills #OpenStandard #AAIF #LinuxFoundation

Source: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation

item.title: Modular Agent Skills and New Evaluators Enable Precise Performance Measurement
item.description:
Modular Agent Skills and New Evaluators Enable Precise Performance Measurement

General‑purpose AI agents can handle many tasks, but keeping them aligned with business procedures—such as compliance checks, document‑processing workflows, escalation policies, and engineering conventions—gets difficult when all rules are baked into a single system prompt or application logic.

🔍 Overview

  • Encoding every procedure in one prompt becomes hard to maintain and update.
  • Skills provide a modular alternative that isolates domain‑specific guidance from the agent’s core.
  • The open Agent Skills standard makes skills portable across compatible harnesses, allowing an agent to load only the skill it needs at runtime.

🧩 How Skills Work

A skill is a reusable set of instructions, typically stored in a SKILL.md file, that teaches an agent a specific task (e.g., redacting a contract, reconciling an invoice, or following pull‑request conventions). Each skill packages the tools and context required for correct execution.

Component Description
Instructions Domain‑specific guidance and constraints injected into the agent’s context
Tool bindings APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or local commands the skill depends on
Knowledge Reference material and worked examples
Workflow Multi‑step procedure or decision logic the skill follows
Guardrails Format requirements, scope limits, and validation rules

Benefits of the modular approach

  • Faster specialization of agents
  • Reuse of proven procedures across agents and workflows
  • Consistent behavior without fine‑tuning the underlying model
  • Easy updates to domain‑specific guidance without rewriting core logic

⚙️ New Evaluation Capabilities

Skill composability introduces two failure modes that standard output‑quality metrics miss:

  1. The agent invokes an inappropriate skill for the task.
  2. The agent invokes the correct skill but skips or only partially follows its instructions. Both can produce fluent, plausible responses that lack the required domain knowledge, so evaluating the final response alone is insufficient.

To measure these failures, Strands Evals SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations add three skill‑focused evaluators:

  • Skill Selection Accuracy – Checks whether each invoked skill was appropriate for the task. Returns a binary result per skill.
  • Skill Instruction Following – Rates how fully the agent followed the skill’s prescribed steps. Returns a five‑level rating grounded in evidence for each step.
  • SkillInvoked – Deterministic check that a named skill was loaded successfully. Calls no model and is specific to Strands Evals.

🚀 Using the Evaluators

  1. An agent receives a task and a catalog of skills, selects a skill, loads it, and acts.
  2. The run is recorded as a trajectory in Strands Evals or as an OpenTelemetry trace in the observability layer.
  3. The recorded record can be fed to all three evaluators.
  4. Prompt templates and rubrics for Skill Selection Accuracy and Skill Instruction Following are available in the prompt‑template documentation.
  5. The AgentCore CLI provides commands to run the evaluators, add deterministic routing checks to a test suite, and interpret per‑skill results to guide fixes.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Teams can detect mismatched skill usage early, before erroneous outputs reach users.
  • Instruction‑following gaps are surfaced with concrete evidence, enabling targeted remediation.
  • The deterministic SkillInvoked check guarantees that a skill was actually loaded, removing ambiguity from test results.
  • Overall, the combination of modular skills and dedicated evaluators improves reliability, maintainability, and auditability of AI‑driven business processes.

#AIAgents #AgentSkills #Evaluation #AmazonBedrock #StrandsEvals

Source: Evaluate skill-equipped agents with Strands Evals and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
